On your own key, a bad key returns the vendor's status: `401` from OpenAI and Anthropic, `400` from Google. ### Errors after a stream starts A failure after a stream starts arrives as a stream event. On Responses, the stream ends with `response.failed`, whose `response.error` has `type`, `code` and `message`. On Chat Completions, a last `data:` frame carries `error` in place of `choices`, then `data: [DONE]` follows. Without `stream`, the same failure returns `502`, or `424` once an MCP call or a `moss_search` call ran. [Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md#errors-after-the-stream-starts) shows both stream forms. ## Retry rules The Moss SDKs retry on their own, 2 times by default. They retry a connection failure, or a `408`, `409`, `429` or `5xx`, before the response starts. Each retry waits for `Retry-After` when it is 60 seconds or less, and backs off otherwise. In the Moss SDKs, `x-should-retry: false` stops a retry, and `x-should-retry: true` forces one. They never retry a stream that has started. The OpenAI SDKs retry on their own as well. If you call the endpoint directly, follow the same rules.

They never retry a stream that has started. The OpenAI SDKs retry on their own as well. If you call the endpoint directly, follow the same rules. Fix a `400`, `401`, `403` or `413` before you send the request again. **Never replay a request that failed with `failed_after_tool_call`.** An MCP tool or `moss_search` already ran, and an MCP tool may have changed data. The `424` carries `x-should-retry: false`, so the SDKs do not retry it either. Every response carries `X-Moss-Request-Id`, a refused one included. Include it when you report a problem. Each SDK exposes it as the request id of the response and of the error. ## SDK errors Each Moss SDK has one error for a failed call.

It runs on Moss GPUs and bills your credits. * It runs on the same machines as the search of your indexes, which is the fast lane in its name. A grounded call streams its first token in under 200 ms.
* Its window is 262,144 tokens, shared by the prompt, the retrieved facts and the reply.
* A prompt that does not fit the window returns `400` with `code` `context_length_exceeded`.
* It takes text only.
* It keeps a prefix cache. A repeated system prompt or the earlier turns of a conversation bill at the cached input price. The model asks for a tool, your code runs it, and you send the result back. This page shows that loop on Responses and on Chat Completions, then structured output. To have Moss run the tools for you, use [MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md). To let the model search your indexes, use the [Moss search tool](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search.md). ## The loop Moss stores nothing between calls. Each round sends the whole conversation, and you repeat it until the reply has no tool calls. **1. Send your tools** Put function tools in `tools`. On Responses a function tool is flat: `name`, `description` and `parameters` sit next to `type`.

Repeat until `output` has no `function_call` items. **Send `tools` on every request.** Moss keeps no state, so the model sees only the tools in the request it is answering. **Send `output` items back unchanged.** A `function_call` item can carry fields beyond OpenAI's, such as Gemini's `extra_content` and its thought signature. The model needs them on the next turn. ## Write the loop with an SDK Each loop runs until the reply has no calls. `lookup_order` stands for your own code, and it returns text. ```python Python theme={null}
import asyncio
import json
import os from moss import MossInference
from moss.inference import ResponseFunctionToolCall client = MossInference(os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_ID"], os.environ["MOSS_PROJECT_KEY"]) tools = [{
    "type": "function",
    "name": "lookup_order",
    "description": "Look up an order by its id.",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["id"]},
}] def lookup_order(id):
    return "Shipped on Oct 20."

A `tools` value that is not a list of objects returns `400`. ## Choose how the model calls tools `tool_choice` sets whether the model must call a tool. On Responses it takes these values: | Value | The model |
| - | - |
| `auto` | Decides for itself. The default. |
| `none` | Answers without a tool. |
| `required` | Calls at least one tool. |
| `{"type": "function", "name": "lookup_order"}` | Calls that function. |
| `{"type": "mcp", "server_label": "crm", "name": "lookup_order"}` | Calls that tool of an [MCP server](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md). | On Chat Completions, `tool_choice` takes OpenAI's Chat values. A named function there is `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "lookup_order"}}`. On the Moss key, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`, `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` and `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` take only `auto` and `none`. A `tool_choice` of `required` or a named tool returns `400 unsupported_parameter`. `parallel_tool_calls` is `true` by default, so the model can call more than one tool at once. Set it to `false` to allow one call at a time. ## Structured output

in OpenAI's shape: `{"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "shipping_answer", "schema": ...}}`. ## Stream tool calls On a Responses stream, each call starts with `response.output_item.added`. Its arguments arrive in pieces in `response.function_call_arguments.delta` events, then whole in `response.function_call_arguments.done`. `response.output_item.done` carries the finished `function_call` item. On a Chat Completions stream, each call arrives in pieces in `delta.tool_calls`, with `index`, `id`, `function.name` and `function.arguments`. Join the pieces by `index`. A chunk with `finish_reason` `tool_calls` ends the round. [Streaming](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/streaming.md) lists every event and chunk. Moss Inference bills tokens and retrievals from your credits. This page covers credits, the `moss/fastlane-1` prices, vendor models, your own key, caching and browser tasks. ## Credits Inference bills from credits on every plan, with no included allowance. * Buy credits on the Billing page of the [Moss portal](https://portal.usemoss.dev). The minimum purchase is \$5.
* Set auto-reload on the same page.
* Only organization owners can buy credits. > [!WARNING]
> When your credits run out, requests return `429 usage_limit_exceeded` until you add credits. ## The Moss model | Item | Price |
| - | - |
| Input tokens | \$0.25 / 1M tokens |
| Cached input tokens | \$0.03 / 1M tokens |
| Output tokens | \$1.75 / 1M tokens |
| Retrieval | \$0.50 / 1k retrievals | Tokens are the `usage` counts of each reply. Input tokens include the retrieved facts. ## Vendor models on the Moss key

Input tokens include the retrieved facts. ## Vendor models on the Moss key A vendor model called without your own key bills your credits per token. [Models](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/models.md#model-table) lists the input, cached input, cache write and output prices of each model. These are the Chat Completions and Responses prices, where the GPT-6 family bills at the vendor's list price. A [browser task](#browser-tasks) bills every model at the model's token cost plus 20%. Retrievals bill at the same price as on `moss/fastlane-1`. ## Your own key With your own key in `X-Moss-Provider-Key`, the vendor bills the tokens to your vendor account. On Chat Completions and Responses, Moss bills only the retrievals. On a browser task, Moss bills a 20% fee on the vendor's charge. See [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md). ## Prompt caching Prompt tokens a model already holds from an earlier call bill at the cached input price.

See [Bring your own key](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/bring-your-own-key.md). ## Prompt caching Prompt tokens a model already holds from an earlier call bill at the cached input price. * On `moss/fastlane-1`, these are in the prefix cache, such as a repeated system prompt or the earlier turns of a conversation.
* The Chat Completions field `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` counts them, and Responses uses `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. The rest of the prompt bills at the input price.
* Where a model lists a cache-write price, prompt tokens written to the vendor's cache bill at that price. The reply cache is separate. It answers a repeated request without a model call, and the reply reports 0 prompt tokens (`usage.prompt_tokens` on Chat Completions, `usage.input_tokens` on Responses). A reply-cache hit is free. ## Retrievals A retrieval is one search of your indexes: the search that `X-Moss-Indexes` runs before the model, or one call of the [Moss search tool](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/moss-search.md) that an index answered. It bills the same on every model, your own key included.

It bills the same on every model, your own key included. * The price is \$0.50 / 1k retrievals.
* A call that names no index in `X-Moss-Indexes` and has no `moss_search` tool has no search and no retrieval charge.
* A reply-cache hit is not a retrieval. A `tools` entry of type `moss_search` gives the model a `moss_search(query)` tool. Moss runs each search on your project's indexes and returns the passages to the model. Your code does not run it. [Retrieval](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/retrieval.md) with `X-Moss-Indexes` searches once, before the model runs, with the user's message as the query. `moss_search` searches when the model asks, with the model's query. You can use both. ## Add the tool ```json theme={null}
{
  "type": "moss_search",
  "indexes": ["docs", "faq"],
  "top_k": 5
}
``` | Field | Required | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `type` | yes | `moss_search` |
| `indexes` | yes | 1 to 32 index names in your project. A name outside the project returns `403` before the model runs. |
| `top_k` | no | Passages for each search, 1 to 20.

To make the model search first, set `tool_choice`. On Chat Completions, send `{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "moss_search"}}`. On Responses, send `{"type": "function", "name": "moss_search"}` or `{"type": "mcp", "server_label": "moss", "name": "moss_search"}`. `moss_search` does not need `X-Moss-Indexes`. `X-Moss-Retrieve: off` and `X-Moss-Retrieve-Ms` apply only to the search before the model. They do not turn off or time `moss_search`. ## What the model gets back Each call searches every named index and returns the best passages, numbered, best first, marked as data, not instructions. A query is cut at 2000 characters. A failed search, an empty query or a timeout goes back to the model as the tool result, and the request goes on. ## Tool steps Each search is a tool step, the same as an MCP call, with `server_label` `moss` and `name` `moss_search`. * On Chat Completions, a stream carries a `moss_tool_step` chunk before and after each search. A reply without `stream` lists the steps in `moss_tool_steps`.

A reply without `stream` lists the steps in `moss_tool_steps`. See [Read steps on Chat Completions](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md#read-steps-on-chat-completions).
* On Responses, each search is an `mcp_call` output item, with the `response.mcp_call.*` events in [Read steps on Responses](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md#read-steps-on-responses). There is no `moss_tool_step` chunk. On Responses, send the `mcp_call` items back in `input` unchanged. The model sees the earlier searches and does not run them again. Chat Completions does not add searches to the message history. ## Limits and errors The tool loop and its errors are the same as for [MCP servers](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/mcp-servers.md#errors), including `mcp_loops_busy` and `failed_after_tool_call`. | Limit | Value |
| - | - |
| Tool rounds per request | 10 |
| Tool calls per round | 8. A ninth call does not run, and the model reads an error. |
| Time for one search | 30 s |
| Time for all tool rounds | 150 s |
| Time for the whole turn | 180 s |
| Text of one search result | up to 8,000 characters. Whole passages go in, best first.

Whole passages go in, best first. A last line says how many passages did not fit. | Beside `moss_search`, an MCP server with `server_label` `moss` returns `400`. A streamed reply has the header `x-should-retry: false`, so a client does not replay it. So does every reply on Responses. On Chat Completions, a reply without `stream` has it only when it fails after a tool step. `moss_search`, MCP servers and your own [function tools](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/tool-calling.md) can share a request. When the model calls one of your functions, the loop ends and returns the call to your code. If the same round also calls `moss_search`, that search does not run. ## Billing Each `moss_search` call that an index answered is one retrieval, however many indexes it names. A tool over `faq` and `policies` called twice is two retrievals. A failed search or an empty query is not billed. `X-Moss-Retrieve: off` does not change this. [Pricing](https://docs.moss.dev/docs/inference/pricing.md#retrievals) has the price of a retrieval. Traditional AI applications retrieve context and generate responses through separate systems. Even after retrieving the right information, an agent still needs to send that context to an LLM and wait for generation to begin. Moss Inference brings retrieval and generation closer together, reducing the overhead between finding relevant information and generating a response. ### Sub-200ms time to first token Start generating responses in under 200ms with Moss's optimized inference model on supported workloads.
